newsitem.title: UK: Argentine general in first British post-war visit.
newsitem.headline: Argentine general in first British post-war visit.

text.p: General Martin Balza on Monday became the first chief of the Argentine military to visit Britain since the two countries went to war over the Falkland Islands in 1982.

Balza, who fought as an artillery officer in the South Atlantic conflict, is seeing British defence chiefs and visiting garrisons as the two former foes cement closer ties after the 1990 resumption of diplomatic links.
"This is a military visit, not a political one. He is here to warm contacts on the military front," said a British defence official. "It is helpful in developing relations further."
Argentine officials also saw the highly symbolic three-day visit by the chief of staff of the armed services as a confidence-building exercise.
Balza is the highest ranking officer to travel to London since the war. He was the only top commander to survive a shake-up of Argentina's military high command last month.
Britain and Argentina fought a 10-week war over the remote islands in 1982. About 1,000 servicemen died after Britain sent a task force to dislodge Argentine troops.
Buenos Aires wants Britain to lift an arms embargo which it has called anachronistic, arguing it harms British industry more than Argentina's armed forces.
But the British government last month firmly denied press reports suggesting it had agreed to relax the arms embargo in exchange for a deal on oil exploration around the Falklands.
Anglo-Argentine relations improved markedly in September 1995 when the two countries announced agreement on a complicated deal on hydrocarbons exploration in waters around the islands.

But Argentine oil giant YPF SA failed to win a licence for oil exploration when the tender outcome was announced last month. The Argentine government, which maintains a stake in YPF, said it was confident there was no hidden agenda.
